title: Operations Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Evaluate technology in operations, judge process choices and analyse efficiency data.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — technology in operations, efficiency analysis and operational decisions.
final_note: You can evaluate the role of technology, judge process choices and analyse efficiency data.

concepts.def: Machines doing work previously done by humans
Continuous small improvements by all staff
Total cost divided by units produced
Slowest stage that limits total output
Total Quality Management — everyone owns quality
Probability a product works without failing

walkthroughs.body_html:
Automation raises productivity and consistency but cuts jobs and needs capital.

Expect short-term redundancies and retraining costs against long-term savings.
Unit cost = total cost ÷ units made. As output rises with the same fixed costs, unit cost falls — economies of scale.

An exam case may show productivity rising but defect rates also rising.

Top answers spot the trade-off: pushing speed often hurts quality unless you invest in training and QA.

numericals.q: Fixed costs £20,000. Variable cost £4 per unit. 4,000 units made. What is unit cost, in £?
